_comment: Spite is fractured by the loop — the only other person who half-remembers the resets. Two halves, neither of them a villain: one wants you out, one has decided the loop is safer. Their unpredictability is the player's first hard evidence that the loop is real.

spite.name: Spite

alters.name: the one who remembers you
alters.line: Their face is doing the open thing. This is the half that wants you out.

alters.name: the one who remembers the endings
alters.line: Their face is doing the closed thing. This is the half that has watched you fail more times than you have been alive.

events.text: "You always stop here," they say, and shove you bodily forward. "Not this time. Go on."
They press something into your hand without explaining it and are gone before you can ask.
"Left at the fork. Trust me, I've done this bit four hundred times."
They sit with you a minute and say nothing at all, and somehow that is the useful thing.
"It doesn't matter," they say, very reasonably, and while you are arguing they go through your pack.
They take something of yours and will not say which. You find out later.
"Stay. It's warm here and tomorrow is the same anyway." You lose an hour to the conversation.
They walk you the wrong way on purpose, cheerfully, all the way to a wall.

spite.warded: You brace for it — and the Tonic does its work. Whichever half of them arrived, they think better of it and wander off.
